item.title: TapeUp 0.1.5
item.description:
What's new

  • TapeUp remembers voices. Name a voice once, and later meetings fill that name in by themselves. A filled-in name says so: listen, and leave it if it's right, or pick someone else. When you fix one, TapeUp shows earlier meetings where it made the same guess, for you to check. The voices it remembers stay on your Mac.
  • Free up space. Free Up Space… in the ··· menu lists the recordings that still hold their audio, filtered by age. The ones that lose their audio are listed first, with the same count and size as the button. Lock any recording to keep its audio. Recordings without a transcript or labeled speakers wait until they have them.
  • Rename someone everywhere. Renaming a person on the People page carries through every recording and their remembered voice, with Undo.
  • Naming a voice adds them to who was there, and a new name joins your people list.
  • More for your agent. The command line can now import a file (it transcribes and labels speakers too), list and name voices, keep the people list, remove audio, and lock audio. Your agent can lock audio but never unlock it. Run /Applications/TapeUp.app/Contents/MacOS/TapeUp help.

Install

Download TapeUp.dmg below and drag TapeUp to Applications, or:

brew install kkyrian/tap/tapeup

Already on TapeUp? It updates itself when you're not recording, or use Check for Updates… in the ··· menu.

item.title: TapeUp 0.1.4
item.description:
What's new

  • Keep the transcript, drop the audio. Once a recording has a transcript, the new button beside the trash removes only the audio and keeps everything else, with Undo right there. Handy for meetings you only need in writing. Right-click a recording for the same thing.
  • Transcript-only recordings say so. The card reads "Transcript only", and lists show a small page mark before the length.
  • The trash says what it takes: the recording and its transcript.

Install

Download TapeUp.dmg below and drag TapeUp to Applications, or:

brew install kkyrian/tap/tapeup

Already on TapeUp? It updates itself when you're not recording, or use Check for Updates… in the ··· menu.

item.title: TapeUp 0.1.3
item.description:
What's new

  • Speakers are labeled on their own. Once a recording's transcript is ready, TapeUp finds who spoke when, so there's nothing extra to click. Imports still follow their Label speakers switch.
  • You're among the names. The name you set on the People page comes first when you say who was there and when you name a voice. It's offered, not assumed, so you can leave yourself out of a meeting you missed.
  • Open at login starts on for new installs. Turn it off in Settings any time.
  • The floating timer stays on one line past an hour.

Install

Download TapeUp.dmg below and drag TapeUp to Applications, or:

brew install kkyrian/tap/tapeup

Already on TapeUp? It updates itself when you're not recording, or use Check for Updates… in the ··· menu.

  • The import bar moves while a file copies. Bringing in one long recording, the bar at the bottom of the Import window now fills as it copies, instead of waiting at zero until the file is done.

item.title: TapeUp 0.1.0
item.description:
The first release of TapeUp, a meeting recorder for Mac, built for you and your AI agent.

What it does

  • Records both sides of a call in any app: your voice and everything your Mac plays. No bot joins the call. Press ⌥⌘R mid-call to start, and small controls float over your windows to pause or stop.
  • Transcribes on your Mac while you talk, in 52 languages.
  • Knows who said what. Label speakers finds each voice, with a line it said and a button to hear it.
  • Says who was there. Tap how many were on the call and type a few letters of each name.
  • Names your recordings. Pick Claude Code or Codex in Settings and it titles each recording and suggests who was there. It stays off until you pick one; without it, Apple Intelligence titles them where your Mac has it.
  • Brings in old recordings from files or folders, transcribed with progress and the time left.
  • Finds any meeting by its title, the people in it, or the words said.
  • Hands it to your agent. Every recording is a folder of plain files with an AGENTS.md, and TapeUp has a command line agents can use.
  • Keeps going when AirPods connect or disconnect mid-call, and writes audio as it records, so a crash keeps the meeting.

Recording and transcription stay on your Mac. Only the agent you pick sees a transcript.

Install

Download TapeUp.dmg below and drag TapeUp to Applications, or:

brew install kkyrian/tap/tapeup

TapeUp isn't notarized by Apple, so macOS stops it the first time. Click Done, then Open Anyway next to TapeUp in System Settings › Privacy & Security. It downloads its speech model once (2.3 GB, or 680 MB on Macs with less than 16 GB of memory).

Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later; tested on macOS 27.

Updates

TapeUp checks once a day and installs updates when you're not recording. Turn that off under Settings › Automatic updates, or use Check for Updates… in the ··· menu.
